title: Blackhole Tracker: BHSM Boundary Interpretation of Compact-Lens Mass, Motion, and Conditional Response

authors.name: Norman P. Carberry

abstract: Blackhole Tracker interprets compact-lens inference as Berger–Hopf Standard Model (BHSM) gravitational surface topography, counting one exterior once. App, command-line, Python and notebook interfaces support resolved pairs and native photometry. A frozen pilot processes 100 OGLE-III events and 76,344 measurements: 89 fail its adequacy screen, eleven are not rejected and two pass stricter archival follow-up criteria. An atlas adds 59 published parallax events, retaining 155 distinct source/event directions and failed assessments. Three qualified or disputed targets remain unconfirmed. Mass, lens position, distance and absolute motion remain unresolved; duration is not mass. A joint benchmark retains 12,521 photometric measurements and 21 two-coordinate HST positions: three Gaussian noise candidates fail residual checks; a normalized Student experiment remains numerically unresolved. Corrections remove numerical-reference dependence, admit physical nuisance profiles and preserve unavailable motion uncertainties. A frozen synthetic study retains 4,608 datasets and 4,736 fits; three photometric uncertainty-calibration tests fail alongside successful conditional resolved controls. The optional scalar–tensor calculation bounds retained boundary states, but two projected modes vanish and the leading response is degenerate with shear. The product supports auditable screening and conditional response tests. No new black-hole identification, independent known-black-hole recovery, measured BHSM core dynamics, independently detected R1 deformation or horizon classification is established.
